title: Schottky versus super Schottky in genus 4
summary: The study of super Riemann surfaces and their moduli led Witten and Felder, Kazhdan and Polishchuk to ask what is the smallest $d$ such that the $d$-th power of the Schottky ideal is contained in the super Schottky ideal. Felder, Kazhdan and Polishchuk proved that $d=g$ in odd genus $g\geq5$ and that $d\in\{g-1,g\}$ in even genus $g\geq4$; Y.~Shen subsequently proved that $d=g$ in even genus $g\geq6$. Thus the only remaining open case was $g=4$. Here we close this gap by showing that in genus $4$ too, the smallest power of the Schottky ideal contained in the super Schottky ideal is $d=g=4$.…
